newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KITE CONCERNED OVER MICKELSON, LOVE RYDER CUP STATUS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KITE CONCERNED OVER MICKELSON, LOVE RYDER CUP STATUS.

text.p: U.S. Ryder Cup captain Tom Kite expressed concern Wednesday that Cup veterans Phil Mickelson and Davis Love might fail to automatically qualify for the team.

With just three PGA Tour events left before the American team that will take on Europe at Valderrama in September is finalised, Mickelson and Love are precariously perched ninth and 10th in the U.S. Ryder Cup standings.
The top 10 players automatically qualify for the team.

"At one stage early this year, Phil was third and Davis was fourth. I thought they would have had their spots locked up long ago," Kite said Wednesday on the eve of the Sprint International at Castle Pines.

Previous Ryder Cup experience is a highly valued commodity in the emotionally charged competition and will be at a premium on a U.S. squad that looks like it will have at least five Ryder rookies in the mix in Tiger Woods, newly-crowned British Open champin Justin Leonard, Jim Furyk, Scott Hoch and Tommy Tolles.

Mickelson, with one Ryder Cup under his belt, and Love, a a member of two Ryder teams, have played well lately. But the pair have slipped down the standings because other players have performed better.
Kite does have two captain's picks to complete the 12-man squad, but having to use them on Love or Mickelson, should they slip out of the top 10, would force him into a difficult position.
Kite wasn't tipping his hand, but it is believed that Fred Couples (currently 16th) and Tom Watson (17th) are among the players he is seriously considering on his "very short" list.

It is obvious Kite does not want to be forced to choose between Mickelson, Love, Couples and Watson, just as European captain Seve Ballesteros does not want to have to omit either Nick Faldo, Jose Maria Olazabal or Jesper Parnevik.
Kite will announce his two selections following the PGA Championship next month at Winged Foot.
No matter what the final makeup of his team, Kite insists that Europe should be considered favourites to defend the Cup because of its players greater familiarity with Valderrama.
Only three of the likely U.S. team members -- Woods, Mark O'Meara and Love -- have played the course.
"Valderrama requires more local knowledge than perhaps any course I've ever seen, apart from Augusta National," Kite said.
"The two times I've been there I've played in different winds, and I could not believe the difference where you drove the ball. The course changed dramatically."
Kite, a veteran of seven Ryder Cups with a 15-9-4 record, is currently 29th in the standings but refused to concede he could not make the team.
He pointed out that if he won here and at the PGA Championship in two weeks he would easily qualify.
